ns2:section.sectionText: DEVELOPMENT ECONOMICS: examines microeconomic development issues in poor countries. We examine research on health, cash transfers, early childhood development, education, risk-sharing, and the causes and welfare impacts of conflict. Much of the focus is on using empirical methods to measure the causal impact of development programs. We study specific programs that have worked in improving health/education/child outcomes and we discuss how economists evaluate the effectiveness of these programs. Prerequisites: Econ 500, Econ 502, and enrolled in Econ 503 in the current semester.
